correctness.rationale: The binary Baum–Sweet prefix starts b(0)=1 and b(n)=1 precisely when ordinary binary zero runs have even lengths. Adjacent ones occur iff n=4^t-1, with no triple ones, by following even last-zero-run parity under increment. The standard shortest complete-two-letter greedy arch decomposition exactly computes scattered-subsequence universality, as its constructive lower embedding and missing length-(a+1) word upper bound show. After initial word 110110 (four ones, two arches), a further one completes an arch unless it ends a pair of adjacent ones, when the second one requires the next zero. The only trailing pairs occur at prefix N=4^t+1; small N=0..6 checked. Thus for all N>=4, U=B-2-1_exception. The accepted positive binaries form 1(1|00)*, yielding count F_ell at bit-length ell and B(2^m)=F_{m+2}; monotonicity brackets all N to give Θ(N^log2φ), with exact dyadic limit φ²/sqrt5. Independently regenerated bits and greedy arches agreed for each N<=16384 and Fibonacci dyadic levels through 14; these are bounded checks supporting a full symbolic proof.
